topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by connecting it to the practicals and outlining its learning outcomes.

topics.label: Tumor virology and the discovery of cellular proto-oncogenes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how research into cancer-causing viruses revealed that transformation originates in altered cellular genes.

topics.label: Experimental tests of cellular transformation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how experimental assays establish whether genes and mutations confer transformed properties on cells.

topics.label: Functional classification and effects of cancer mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer mutations are classified by their functional effects, using checkpoint regulation and mutation dominance to illustrate and qualify those classifications.

topics.label: Genetic instability and defective DNA repair
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish sequence from chromosomal instability and explain how failures of DNA repair produce these abnormalities.

topics.label: Genetic instability from replication and mitotic errors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how failures to copy and segregate the genome faithfully during cell division generate instability in cancer cells.

topics.label: Mutation order in colorectal cancer progression
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how the timing of mutation acquisition, particularly the onset of genetic instability, shapes colorectal tumor progression.

topics.label: Hereditary cancer predisposition and the changing role of inherited defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how inherited tumor-suppressor defects predispose to cancer while showing that a defect contributing to tumor development need not remain necessary for malignancy.

topics.label: Closing, further reading and questions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by inviting questions, recommending reading and previewing the next lecture.
